title: Understanding N-grams
text: Think about how N-grams work. They capture sequences of letters, but do they consider the biological significance of codons?

title: Codons and Amino Acids
text: Remember, codons are groups of $$3$$ letters that translate into amino acids. How might this affect the usefulness of N-grams?

title: N-gram Overlap
text: Consider how N-grams might break down a sequence like ATGCA. What overlapping segments would it create?

hintAnswer: It could suggest incorrect sequences like AGA from ATGCA.
title: Non-consecutive Segments
text: If N-grams capture non-consecutive segments, what might be a potential issue with this?
choices: It could suggest incorrect sequences like AGA from ATGCA.
It could capture too many sequences.

title: Wrap-around Segments
text: DNA sequences do not wrap around. How might N-grams mistakenly capture segments that seem to wrap around?
